attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Join Prometheus target health to the 9 static fleet nodes by private IP (plan.md:100-105).
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: Every FLEET.md node appears in Prometheus targets under its 10.20.0.x address, so an absent target really means the exporter is down.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: db-mon-1's exporter is up but scraped as host.docker.internal:9100, so the plan's 'absent -> red with no node_exporter target' rule paints db-mon-1 red on day one while the same 9 targets are 9/9 up. The node table and the Prometheus card disagree, and '9/9 nodes' is unreachable.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: If the scrape config carries a node/host label, the join could be fixed without changing the address. The evidence file shows instances only; /api/v1/targets labels were not read.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: NFS mount hangs (one dependency down) while the health page auto-refreshes (plan.md:62, 67-70, 156-157).
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: The 1200 ms race contains the damage of a blocked statfs to the health request that triggered it.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: plan.md:156-157 'the request thread may stay until the mount recovers'; server/admin/api.js:160 'const stat = await fs.stat(storeFile);'; server/app.js:108 'express.static(dist, {'.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: fs.promises.statfs runs on libuv's threadpool (default 4 threads). Promise.race/AbortSignal time out the promise, not the kernel call. With a 5 s cache a new statfs starts every 5 s, so ~20 s of a hung mount exhausts the pool and queues every fs and getaddrinfo in the web process behind it - including the static assets and store mtime read the capture page needs. The health page degrades the tier it monitors; the plan's own weakness note understates this as one stranded request.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: Mount options are not in the repo. A soft mount with timeo well under 1200 ms would make the accumulation rare; a hard mount makes it near-certain.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Add GET /healthz to the socket process's plain createServer callback without breaking Engine.IO (plan.md:72-84, server/socket/index.js:20-23).
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: Engine.IO leaves the original request listener in place for non-/socket.io paths, so a /healthz branch there is safe.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: node_modules/engine.io/build/server.js:674-691 saves the existing 'request' listeners, removeAllListeners, intercepts path matches and delegates the rest; node_modules/socket.io/dist/index.js:327-345 does the same for client serving.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: The delegation is explicit in the installed libraries. A /healthz branch in the original callback is only reached for non-Engine.IO paths; the plan's claim that Engine.IO paths are untouched holds.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: Verified against the installed engine.io/socket.io versions only; a major upgrade could change the wrapping.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Workers check '>= 1 per expected role' (plan.md:48) fed from WorkerPool.snapshot().
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: The pool can attribute connected workers to expected roles (download vs OCR).
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: python/worker/__main__.py:56 'self.emitter.send("worker:ready", {"slots": self.slots()})'; server/socket/worker-pool.js:1450-1456 stores only {socket, slots, connectedAt}; server/socket/admin.js:90 emits pool.slotStats() = {workers, auth, export, queued}.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: No hostname, node id or role ever reaches the pool. Role coverage cannot be computed; the check collapses to a total count (hardcoded 7, which drifts) and cannot say which role/node is missing - the page's stated purpose for the worker tier.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: socket.handshake.address might carry the mesh IP and could be mapped back to fleet.js roles, if workers connect directly rather than through a proxy; not verified live.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: 5 s cache plus 15 s auto-refresh cannot amplify probe load (plan.md:69-70, 118).
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: The refresh cadence multiplies probes into a load problem.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: plan.md:69-70 'Results are cached for 5 s ...'; plan.md:118 'auto-refresh every 15 s, paused when the tab is hidden'; evidence-fleet.txt:41 one account, 7 workers.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: One admin cookie and one account: at most ~12 collectHealth batches/minute, 9 concurrent probes each, worst case ~1200 ms. Network probe load is negligible; the amplification risk is the statfs threadpool, not request count.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: The cache is per process and per tab refresh, so N open tabs scale linearly - still trivial at N<=10.

attempted_counterexamples.scenario: Gate check: does 'status endpoint answers' prove the gate works once the :4100 provider exists (plan.md:41, 46, 158-159)?
attempted_counterexamples.assumption: A green gate row means the gate is usable, so the current red is meaningful and will clear when the provider ships.
attempted_counterexamples.evidence: server/gate.js:528-540 status() returns {ok:true, reason:'status_error'} on a network error (fails open); server/gate.js:637-651 the redeem path is what decoys a ?g= visitor and is never exercised by a status probe.
attempted_counterexamples.observed: The plan probes /api/status, the one gate call that already fails open. A provider with working status and broken redeem reads green while every token-holder is still decoyed; the day-one red only proves nothing listens, not that redeem works. The plan admits this in section 7, so it is a known overclaim rather than a discovery.
attempted_counterexamples.uncertainty: The provider does not exist, so no live contract (status body, secret, HTTP codes) can be tested. The probe mirrors gate.js's own postJson shape, which is the best available evidence.

reason: The shape is right and Engine.IO/refresh attacks fail, but two facts are wrong as written: db-mon-1 is scraped as host.docker.internal, so the private-IP join shows a permanent false red on the node the page exists to explain; and a hung NFS statfs consumes a shared threadpool thread per refresh, so the health page can stall the web tier it reports on. Both are cheap to fix before building.
